name: Ján Botto
bio: Ján Botto (1829-1881) was a Slovak Romantic poet, born in Vyšný Skálnik in the Gemer region. He belonged to the generation of the Slovak national movement of the mid-nineteenth century and wrote in the codified literary Slovak of the Štúr school.

His reputation rests on a small body of work, above all the ballad-epic Smrť Jánošíkova (1862), which makes the Tatra outlaw Jánošík a symbol of freedom, and the ballad Žltá ľalia. The archive carries Smrť Jánošíkova as a work.
